Jaimalram vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:21714) on 14 May,
2024
Author: Kuldeep Mathur

Bench: Kuldeep Mathur [2024:RJ-JD:21714]
 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR  S.B. Criminal Misc(Pet.) No. 6521/2022 Jaimalram S/o Shri Nandram, Aged About 49 Years, R/o 17 Kyd,
Tehsil Khajuwala, District Bikaner.
 ----Petitioner  Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through PP 2. Smt. Sheeladevi W/o Shri Devilal, R/o Sherawala, Ps -  Bahawala, Tehsil Abohar, District Fajilka, Punjab.
 ----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : None present For Respondent(s) : Mr. Laxman Solanki, PP  Mr. Pramod Kumar Mathur  Mr. Rameshwar Soni  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR  ORDER 14/05/2024

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
By way of filing the instant criminal misc. petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C., the petitioner has prayed for the following relief:
"It is, therefore, most humbly prayed that this misc. petition may kindly be allowed and the order dated 13.06.2018 passed by Learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate No-2, Bikaner in Crl Case no 67/2015 (state vs. Rajendra Kumar) and order dated 17.08.2022 passed by Learned Additional Session Judge No-2, Bikaner in Criminal Revision bearing no-14/ 2020 (CIS No- 154/2018) may kindly be quashed and set aside and the Petitioner may be discharged from all the charges."

Briefly stated facts of the case are that respondent No.2- Smt. Sheela Devi lodged an FIR No.330/2012 dated 02.10.2012 at Police Station Sadar, Bikaner, stating inter-alia that the present petitioner hatched a criminal conspiracy with co-accused- Badri Prasad, Rajendra Prasad, Mohan Jaimalram vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:21714) on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32648643/
1 Lal and Ramniwas Gandhi, and in [2024:RJ-JD:21714] (2 of 4) [CRLMP-6521/2022] furtherance thereof, created a false and fabricated sale agreement dated 09.05.2011 in her name and sold her 1/3rd share of agricultural land situated at Chak-16 BD Tehsil Kahjuwala at Murabba No.115/24 at Killa No.1 to 25 totaling 24 Bigha 10 Biswa, to one Pawan Kumar on 01.08.2012.

entities.text: Mohan Jaimalram vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:21714)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said forged sale agreement dated 09.05.2011, it has been mentioned that the complainant against her share in the above agricultural land, has been paid a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- out of the total amount of Rs.7,00,000/- and the balance amount was to be paid later.

The police after making a thorough investigation in connection with the FIR No.330/2012, submitted the challan against the petitioner and other accused persons for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B IPC.
Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.
Learned counsel submitted that in the FIR, grave allegations of having committed the alleged offences, have been levelled against the co- accused Badri Prasad and Rajendra Prasad.
No specific act or omission in commission of the alleged crime has been attributed to the present petitioner.
Learned counsel submitted that the petitioner was merely a witness to the agreement dated 09.05.2011.

Learned counsel further submitted that if the contents of the FIR No. 330/2012 are taken on its face value, then also, no offences under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of IPC are made out against the present petitioner.
It was vehemently submitted that on the face of record, there is no iota of evidence to connect the present petitioner with the alleged offence.

Learned counsel thus prayed that the impugned order [2024:RJ-JD:21714] (3 of 4)
[CRLMP-6521/2022] dated 13.06.2018 passed by the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate No.2, Bikaner, whereby the charges were framed against the petitioner and the order dated 17.08.2012 passed by the learned revisional Court affirming the order of framing of charges against the petitioner, deserves to be quashed and set aside.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate No.2, Bikaner
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Per Contra, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for respondent No.2 have vehemently opposed the submissions made on behalf of the petitioner.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned Public Prosecutor as well as the learned counsel for the complainant.
Perused the material available on record.

Having regard to the rival submissions made at the Bar and considering the documents available on record, this Court prima facie finds that the petitioner has been named in the FIR and the allegation against the present petitioner is that he along with co- accused persons created a forged and fabricated document (sale agreement) which bears thumb impressions of the complainant- respondent No.2.
The accused persons on the basis of the forged documents, sold the agricultural land belonging to the complainant- respondent No.2 to one Pawan Kumar.

The complainant- respondent No.2 came to know about aforesaid illegal acts of the petitioner and the other accused persons only when she received notices from the Court of Additional District and Sessions Judge No.2, Bikaner, with regard to a civil suit filed against her for specific performance of the forged document i.e. sale agreement dated 09.05.2011.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge No.2, Bikaner
entities.label: COURT

] (4 of 4) [CRLMP-6521/2022] Hon'ble

The Supreme Court of India in the case of Sanghi Brothers (Indore) Private Ltd. Vs. Sanjay Choudhary and Ors. reported in 2009 Cr.L.J.
338 has been pleased to hold that the suspicion about an offence and involvement of the accused, is sufficient to frame charges against him.

entities.text:
Sanghi Brothers (Indore) Private Ltd. Vs. Sanjay Choudhary and Ors. reported in 2009 Cr.L.J.
338
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is settled law that quashing of a charge is an exception to the rule of continuous prosecution.
Where the offence is even broadly satisfied, the Court should be more inclined to permit continuation of prosecution rather than its quashing at the initial stage.

Taking into consideration the narrow scope of interference at this stage, the overall factual matrix as well as the documents placed on record, in the opinion of this Court, no cause for making any interference in the impugned orders is made out.
However, the petitioner shall be at liberty to take up all legal issues, at the appropriate stage, before the learned trial Court.

Consequently, the instant criminal misc. petition filed by the petitioner under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is dismissed being devoid of any merit.
Stay application and other applications, if any, also stand dismissed.
(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 394-himanshu/-
